DoorShut is the entered initial state.

contracts.normative_statement: The microwave system must have an initial entry edge into the DoorShut state as its starting state.
contracts.quote: The microwave starts in the DoorShut state.
contracts.reason: Explicit 'starts in the DoorShut state' establishes a required initial pseudostate edge to DoorShut.

contracts.basis: NL1 clause 'remain in DoorShut if a Cancel action is performed'

binding_hints.reason: Cancel action is the stimulus causing retention.

contracts.normative_statement: When a Cancel action is performed in DoorShut, the system must remain in the DoorShut state (self-transition/retention).
contracts.quote: the system can either remain in DoorShut if a Cancel action is performed
contracts.reason: NL1 explicitly requires DoorShut to be retained under a Cancel action guard, a distinct retention obligation from the door-opened endpoint.

contracts.normative_statement: DoorShut must transition to DoorOpen when the door is opened.
contracts.quote: transition to the DoorOpen state when the door is opened
contracts.reason: Explicit endpoint requirement from DoorShut to DoorOpen triggered by door-opened event.

contracts.normative_statement: DoorShut must transition to DoorOpen on the Door Opened event (restated obligation).
contracts.quote: When the Door Opened action occurs in the DoorShut state, the system transitions to the DoorOpen state.
contracts.reason: NL2 restates the DoorShut-to-DoorOpen transition explicitly with the Door Opened event name.

contracts.normative_statement: DoorOpen must transition back to DoorShut when the door is closed.
contracts.quote: The door can be closed to return to the DoorShut state.
contracts.reason: Explicit reverse endpoint from DoorOpen to DoorShut on door-closed event.

contracts.normative_statement: DoorOpen must transition to DoorOpenWithItem when an item is placed inside the microwave.
contracts.quote: placing an item inside the microwave transitions the system to DoorOpenWithItem
contracts.reason: Explicit endpoint requirement for item placement event.

contracts.normative_statement: DoorOpenWithItem must transition back to DoorOpen when the item is removed.
contracts.quote: If the item is removed, the system returns to DoorOpen.
contracts.reason: Explicit reverse endpoint requirement for item removal event.

binding_hints.reason: Additional data condition beyond the door-closed event.

contracts.normative_statement: DoorOpenWithItem must transition to DoorShutWithItem when the door is closed with zero time set.
contracts.quote: the system can transition to DoorShutWithItem if the door is closed with zero time set
contracts.reason: Explicit endpoint requirement conditioned on door closed with zero time set.

contracts.normative_statement: DoorOpenWithItem must transition to ReadytoCook when cooking time is entered.
contracts.quote: or to ReadytoCook if cooking time is entered
contracts.reason: Explicit endpoint requirement conditioned on cooking time entered.

binding_hints.value: door is closed with zero time set

contracts.normative_statement: The two DoorOpenWithItem alternatives (to DoorShutWithItem vs ReadytoCook) must be distinguishable/mutually exclusive based on their guard conditions.
contracts.quote: the system can transition to DoorShutWithItem if the door is closed with zero time set or to ReadytoCook if cooking time is entered
contracts.reason: NL4 presents an either/or choice from one source with distinct guard conditions, requiring mutual exclusivity.

contracts.normative_statement: DoorShutWithItem must transition to DoorOpenWithItem when the door is opened.
contracts.quote: opening the door transitions the system back to DoorOpenWithItem
contracts.reason: Explicit endpoint requirement for door-opened event.

contracts.normative_statement: DoorShutWithItem must transition to ReadytoCook when cooking time is entered.
contracts.quote: entering cooking time takes the system to ReadytoCook
contracts.reason: Explicit endpoint requirement for cooking-time-entered event.

contracts.normative_statement: ReadytoCook must transition to DoorOpenWithItem when the door is opened.

contracts.reason: Explicit effect on the cooking time variable accompanying the Cancel transition.

The retention obligation (i4) is established: the Cancel self-loop on DoorShut exists structurally but can never fire because DoorShut is unreachable and Cancel's consumer set is empty; the rebuttal (local structural correctness) is a different, weaker property and does not rebut the operational-retention failure, so it survives only as an undercutting note under the frontier discipline (kept as survives per the reason's explicit acknowledgment that the candidate may be viewed as subsumed, which is a competent alternative framing, not a full defeat). Obligation i5 (owner default-entry) restates the same underlying defect as i0/i1/i2 and is established with an unsupported backend, consistent with the direct S2 receipts. The DoorOpen->DoorShut missing-transition obligation (i16) is established by a false S2 receipt with no rebuttal offered. The guard-omission obligations (i6, i7, i8) are established by S5-parsed null guards against required independent guards; the event/trigger-carrier alternative is a different typed field and does not rebut a guard-equality contract, so the rebuttal is defeated. The Cooking-entry timer-start action obligation (i17) is established by a false S4 receipt with no competent alternative lifecycle slot supplied. The scenario-style state-after-stimulus obligations (i9, i10, i11, i12) and the derived Cooking-time-entered obligation (i13) and Cancel-return obligation (i14) all lack any executable backend or bound predicate and their dossiers explicitly state the exact post-stimulus outcome is "delegated to a fresh native FCSTM runtime scenario" with no source trace or expected-answer evidence in the dossier itself; this is a genuine unresolved semantic question (unresolved grounding, not an established violation and not a rebutting survival), since no exact transition/effect facts in the supplied dossier settle whether the model retains the target. The timer-variable data-representation obligation (i15) is established: the complete typed inventories are empty (source_variables=[], model_state_actions=[], model_transition_effects=[]), a finite complete-inventory absence for the exactly bound 'timer' locus; the control-skeleton-abstraction rebuttal is acknowledged in the dossier itself as insufficient to provide an observable carrier, so it is defeated.
